messages:
devsec: Heads-up: triaging 3 Go vuln reports that just landed. CVE-2025-4789 (grpc auth header parsing), CVE-2025-4790 (oauth/jwt token validation edge), CVE-2025-4791 (net/http header/chunk parsing). Need prioritization and patch plan. Affected modules: google.golang.org/grpc, golang-jwt/jwt, and stdlib net/http. Impact spans runtime, control-plane, and Private deployments. @eng-runtime @eng-security please weigh in.

alice: Any reproducible exploits or POCs in the vendor advisories?

devsec: Vendor advisory included a minimal POC for the grpc auth header parsing that can lead to auth bypass in a specific header interleaving case. jwt vuln allows `aud` claim bypass when provided as an empty array in some validation code. net/http issue is a header parsing edge with chunked+trailer that can affect route matching. All three have upstream fixes.

ben: Quick mapping: hosted API uses grpc between services; Dedicated nodes expose grpc+net/http at the edge; Private may be running older deps. We should prioritize grpc and jwt for runtime images.

cara: Proposed triage: grpc = P1 (auth bypass), jwt = P1 (token validation bypass), net/http = P2 (request smuggling-esque). P1s: hotfix + canary to 10% traffic, monitor, then roll.

infra-bot: CI: created ticket INF-3145 for runtime image rebuild. Generated PRs: bump grpc to v1.56.0, golang-jwt to v4.0.0. Note: stdlib net/http fix requires Go runtime patch or an edge mitigation; no upstream go1.x release backport available yet.

alice: Can we vendor a patched net/http implementation into our front proxy so we avoid waiting on a Go release? Also need to scan go.mod for transitive grpc pins.

devsec: Vendor/backport is acceptable short-term. For net/http we'll add an edge check to reject ambiguous `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + `Content-Length` combos and normalize trailers at the proxy. That mitigates exploit surface until go patch lands.

sam: Running inventory now: `for d in $(go list -m all); do echo $d; done | grep grpc` — posting results in a minute.

ben: Also consider customer impact: Dedicated customers on older Go runtimes may need an opt-in patched build and advisory. Product/security should prepare comms.

cara: Plan of record: 1) create branch `patch/2025-security-sprint`; 2) bump grpc and jwt in runtime and control-plane; 3) implement net/http guard in front proxy; 4) CI + smoke tests + SBOM update; 5) Canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback window. ETA for initial PRs: 48h.

dependabot: dependabot: opened PR #842 bump google.golang.org/grpc from v1.54.0 to v1.56.0 in /runtime (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842).

alice: I'll review the PR and run local smoke tests against streaming and token flow. Also will update our SBOM and draft advisory to customers with mitigation steps.

sam: Inventory results: runtime uses grpc v1.54.0, control-plane v1.53.2, some third_party vendors still vendor v1.52.0. I'll push a small script to pin them and open follow-up PRs. Command I ran: ```bash
# find modules referencing grpc
grep -R "google.golang.org/grpc" -n || true
```

ben: Who owns the actual rollout windows? @eng-oncall or @platform-release for coordinated canaries?

cara: @eng-oncall handles hotfix rollouts. Platform-release coordinates canary gating and infra tickets. I'll ping both in the release thread.

devsec: Thanks all. I'll open internal advisory and schedule a 30-min warroom at 14:00 UTC tomorrow. Include links to PRs, mitigation checklist, and rollback playbook. If anyone finds a working exploit POC, escalate immediately and mark the thread P0. :thumbsup:
